query: For refractory high-entropy alloys intended as energetic structural materials, what single testable hypothesis identifies an intervention that could improve ductility and uniform deformability without sacrificing high strength or impact-induced energy release? State the proposed intervention, its hypothesized mechanism, the improvement expected relative to the untreated baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, the prior evidence supporting it, and a decisive experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Microalloying a refractory W–Ta–Cr–V–Mo high-entropy alloy with 0.1 at.% boron will segregate boron to grain boundaries, strengthen those interfaces against decohesion, promote uniform slip transfer, and thereby improve room‐temperature ductility by ≥50% without reducing yield strength by more than 5% or diminishing impact‐induced energy release.
generation.material_initial_state: As‐cast equiatomic W–Ta–Cr–V–Mo refractory HEA, average grain size ~50 μm, no microalloying additions.
generation.intervention: Add 0.1 at.% B via a B‐containing master alloy during arc melting.
generation.conditions: Anneal samples at 1200 °C for 1 h, furnace‐cool; perform uniaxial tensile tests at room temperature (strain rate 10⁻³ s⁻¹), Charpy impact tests at room temperature, and drop‐weight impact tests corresponding to ~10 J.
generation.mechanism: B lowers grain‐boundary energy and increases cohesion, delaying intergranular crack nucleation and enabling more homogeneous intragranular slip.
generation.predicted_outcome: Tensile elongation increases from ~6% to ≥9% (≥50% improvement), yield strength remains within ±5% of ~1.1 GPa, and impact‐induced energy release remains within ±5% of ~200 J.
generation.baseline: Untreated W–Ta–Cr–V–Mo HEA: ~6% elongation, ~1.1 GPa yield strength, ~200 J impact energy release.
generation.boundary: Valid for B additions between 0.05–0.2 at.% and annealing temperatures 1100–1300 °C; B >0.2 at.% may form boride precipitates that embrittle boundaries.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate: exact B segregation levels and solubility in this HEA unknown.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two HEA batches (with and without 0.1 at.% B), anneal at 1200 °C/1 h. Characterize B distribution by TEM‐EDS. Perform room‐temperature tensile, Charpy, and drop‐weight impact tests under identical conditions.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: Hypothesis is falsified if (a) elongation improvement <50% (<9% total elongation), (b) yield strength drops >5% below baseline, (c) impact energy release falls >5% below baseline, or (d) B concentration at grain boundaries is below detectable levels (<1 at.%).
